sections: [{"type":"section","name":"Abstract","has_parts":[{"type":"paragraph","value":"Ahmed Salim Ould Sidi (Arabic: أحمد سالم ولد سيدي, 1939 – 26 March 1981) was a Mauritanian military officer and political leader and acting Prime Minister of Mauritania between 28 and 31 May 1979.","links":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language","text":"Arabic"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Salim_Ould_Sidi#cite_note-1"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritania","text":"Mauritanian"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_prime_ministers_of_Mauritania","text":"Prime Minister of Mauritania"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Salim_Ould_Sidi#cite_note-ws-2"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Salim_Ould_Sidi#cite_note-3"}],"citations":[{"identifier":"cite_note-1","text":"[1]"},{"identifier":"cite_note-2","text":"[2]"},{"identifier":"cite_note-3","text":"[3]"}]}]},{"type":"section","name":"Biography","has_parts":[{"type":"paragraph","value":"He took part in the coup d'état that overthrew Mustafa Ould Salek and helped Ahmed Ould Bouceif to become the Prime Minister.","links":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Mauritanian_coup_d'état","text":"coup d'état"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustafa_Ould_Salek","text":"Mustafa Ould Salek"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Ould_Bouceif","text":"Ahmed Ould Bouceif"}]},{"type":"paragraph","value":"After Ould Bouceif died in an airplane crash on 27 May 1979, Ould Sidi temporarily took his place (only for 3 days). On 31 May 1979, Mohamed Khouna Ould Haidalla replaced him and started to gather all political power in his hands. Ould Sidi remained Vice-president and Chief of Military Committee for National Salvation (CMSN) until the beginning of 1980, when Ould Haidalla eliminated all potential counter candidates. Soon he joined the Alliance for a Democratic Mauritania (AMD), connected to former President Moktar Ould Daddah.","links":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Salim_Ould_Sidi#cite_note-4"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohamed_Khouna_Ould_Haidalla","text":"Mohamed Khouna Ould Haidalla"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Committee_for_National_Salvation","text":"Military Committee for National Salvation"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alliance_for_a_Democratic_Mauritania","text":"Alliance for a Democratic Mauritania"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_heads_of_state_of_Mauritania","text":"President"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moktar_Ould_Daddah","text":"Moktar Ould Daddah"}],"citations":[{"identifier":"cite_note-4","text":"[4]"}]},{"type":"paragraph","value":"On 16 March 1981, he staged a coup attempt against Mohamed Khouna with the help of Mohamed Ould Abdelkader, former Air Force Commander. The coup failed and encouraged the President to take a harder course and abandon civil rule. Both Ould Sidi and Ould Abdelkader were executed by firing squad soon after the failed coup.","links":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Mauritanian_coup_attempt","text":"coup attempt"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohamed_Ould_Abdelkader?action=edit&redlink=1","text":"Mohamed Ould Abdelkader"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritania_Islamic_Air_Force","text":"Air Force"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_by_firing_squad","text":"firing squad"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Salim_Ould_Sidi#cite_note-5"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Salim_Ould_Sidi#cite_note-6"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Salim_Ould_Sidi#cite_note-7"}],"citations":[{"identifier":"cite_note-5","text":"[5]"},{"identifier":"cite_note-6","text":"[6]"},{"identifier":"cite_note-7","text":"[7]"}]}]}]

sections: [{"type":"section","name":"Abstract","has_parts":[{"type":"paragraph","value":"Albert Côté (19 January 1927 – 18 April 2020) was a Canadian forestry engineer and politician.","links":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Côté#cite_note-1"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Côté#cite_note-2"}],"citations":[{"identifier":"cite_note-1","text":"[1]"},{"identifier":"cite_note-2","text":"[2]"}]}]},{"type":"section","name":"Biography","has_parts":[{"type":"paragraph","value":"Côté earned degrees in surveying and forest engineering from Université Laval. He began his career working for the Quebec Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food in 1952. He then worked for the Quebec Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources until 1965. In 1965, he began directing forestry operations at Manicouagan and Aux Outardes River Basin Forest Recovery Office, then became president. He held this position until the organization was replaced by the state-owned REXFOR company in 1964. He then became president and CEO of REXFOR in 1979.","links":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Université_Laval","text":"Université Laval"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture,_Fisheries_and_Food_(Quebec)","text":"Quebec Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Energy_and_Natural_Resources_(Quebec)","text":"Quebec Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Côté#cite_note-3"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Côté#cite_note-4"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Côté#cite_note-5"}],"citations":[{"identifier":"cite_note-3","text":"[3]"},{"identifier":"cite_note-4","text":"[4]"},{"identifier":"cite_note-5","text":"[5]"}]},{"type":"paragraph","value":"He became an assistant deputy minister at the Quebec Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources in 1979, then President of Scierie des Outardes, a joint venture between REXFOR and Quebec & Ontario Paper Co., from 1980 to 1983. He returned to the private sector of forestry engineering from 1983 to 1985."},{"type":"paragraph","value":"Côté was the Quebec Liberal Party 's nominee for the Rivière-du-Loup District in the 1985 Quebec general election. He was elected with a majority of votes, allocating 2304. He became Minister Delegate of Forests. He was re-elected in the 1989 Quebec general election with a slightly larger majority and retained his ministerial post. He was promoted to Minister of Forests in 1991.","links":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_Liberal_Party","text":"Quebec Liberal Party"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivière-du-Loup_(electoral_district)","text":"Rivière-du-Loup District"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Quebec_general_election","text":"1985 Quebec general election"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Côté#cite_note-6"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Quebec_general_election","text":"1989 Quebec general election"}],"citations":[{"identifier":"cite_note-6","text":"[6]"}]},{"type":"paragraph","value":"In 1986, Côté implemented a new set of forestry guidelines with the Forest Act. In January 1991, he defended his forestry protection strategy with the document Aménager pour mieux protéger les forêts. This strategy was heard by the Quebec Bureau of Public Hearings on the Environment that same year.","links":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Côté#cite_note-7"}],"citations":[{"identifier":"cite_note-7","text":"[7]"}]},{"type":"paragraph","value":"Côté retired from politics in January 1994, when Daniel Johnson Jr. replaced Robert Bourassa as Premier of Quebec and leader of the Quebec Liberal Party.","links":[{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Johnson_Jr.","text":"Daniel Johnson Jr."},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Bourassa","text":"Robert Bourassa"},{"url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_of_Quebec","text":"Premier of Quebec"}]}]},{"type":"section","name":"Publications","has_parts":[{"type":"list","has_parts":[{"type":"list_item","value":"Revue forestière française (1979)"}]}]}]
